newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares stretch gains, Telebras recoups.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares stretch gains, Telebras recoups.

text.p: Brazilian stocks extended gains and ended the first half of today's session firmer on eased concerns over an alleged cash-for-votes scandal, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most traded stocks rose 2.52 percent to 10,542 points at 1330 local/1630 GMT before the one-hour lunch break.
Market turnover was a moderate 447.1 million reais ($421.7 million).
Telebras preferred, which plunged over four percent Wednesday, jumped 3.16 percent to 133.80 reais.
Analysts said market mood improved after investors weighed the impact of today's new newspaper report on the scandal.
Folha de Sao Paulo daily, which on Wednesday published a story linking Communications Minister Sergio Motta to the alleged scam involving a re-election bill. Motta quickly denied any wrongdoing.

On Thursday, Folha published transcripts of a purported taped conversation in which a congressional deputy allegedly says Motta granted him a television concession in exchange for his vote backing the re-election bill.

"The new report did not worsen the situation as we first thought," said a senior trader, adding that the threat of a congressional inquiry into the alleged scandal also appears to vanish despite the opposition's efforts.
Motta on Wednesday denied any role in the alleged scam.
Brokers said the market could continue rising cautiously, unless speculation of new reports that could broaden the scandal emerges.
